easy.def: A word used to compare two things.
examples: I am taller than you.
A cat is smaller than a dog.
She runs faster than me.

more.def: A word used to compare two things, showing how they are different.
examples: A blue whale is much bigger than an elephant.
I would rather read a book than watch television.
It took us more than an hour to get there.

easy.def: To say you are glad for what someone did.
examples: I thank my friend.
She thanked her aunt.
Let us thank the cook.

more.def: To tell someone that you are grateful for what they have given or done.
examples: We thanked the bus driver for the ride.
I wrote a card to thank my grandmother for the sweater.
The team thanked the fans for cheering.

easy.def: A word you say when someone is kind to you.
examples: Thanks for the gift!
Thanks, Mom.
Thanks for helping.

more.def: A short way to say that you are grateful for something.
examples: Thanks for holding the door for me.
Thanks, I would love a glass of water.
Thanks for the ride to school.

easy.def: Words that show you are glad.
examples: Give thanks to the cook.
She said thanks.
We gave our thanks.

more.def: Words or actions that show you are grateful.
examples: The class sent their thanks to the firefighters who visited.
He gave thanks for the meal before eating.
Many thanks for your help with the project.

easy.def: A holiday in November when families eat a big meal together.
examples: We eat turkey on Thanksgiving.
Thanksgiving is in November.
Family comes for Thanksgiving.

more.def: A holiday in the United States on the fourth Thursday of November, when people give thanks and share a big meal.
examples: Our family eats turkey and pie on Thanksgiving.
We say what we are thankful for at Thanksgiving dinner.
Thanksgiving is celebrated on the fourth Thursday in November.

easy.def: A word for something over there, away from you.
examples: What is that over there?
I like that.
That is my bike.

more.def: A word used to point to a person or thing farther away, or one just mentioned.
examples: Look at that tall building across the street.
That was the best movie I have seen all year.
Did you hear that strange noise outside?

easy.def: A word which links what someone says or thinks to the rest.
examples: I know that you are kind.
She said that lunch is ready.
I hope that it snows.

more.def: A word used to link what someone says or believes to words like say, think, know, or hope.
examples: Scientists believe that the dinosaurs lived millions of years ago.
My brother told me that the game was canceled.
We are glad that you could join our team.

easy.def: A word used before a name for one special thing.
examples: Please close the door.
The dog is asleep.
I ate the apple.

more.def: A word used before a noun to show you mean one particular person or thing that is already known.
examples: The moon was bright last night.
Can you pass me the red marker?
The museum we visited is downtown.

easy.def: A place where you watch movies or plays.
examples: We saw a movie at the theater.
The theater is dark.
Let's go to the theater.

more.def: A building where people go to watch plays, movies or shows.
examples: We watched a movie at the theater.
The school theater has a big stage.
A play is on at the theater tonight.

easy.def: A word that shows something belongs to them.
examples: The kids lost their ball.
Their dog is big.
The birds fed their babies.

more.def: A word used to show that something belongs to or is connected with two or more people or things.
examples: The students put their backpacks on the hooks.
The bears protect their cubs from danger.
Their house is at the end of the road.

easy.def: A word for more than one person or thing.
examples: I saw them play.
Give them the books.
We like them.

more.def: A word used for two or more people, animals, or things when they are not the ones doing the action.
examples: The coach thanked them for their hard work.
I found my gloves, and I put them in my bag.
We watched the geese until we could not see them anymore.

easy.def: The main idea of something.
examples: The theme of the party is space.
The theme of the book is friendship.
The class chose a theme.

more.def: The main idea or subject of a story, party or other event.
examples: The theme of the party was pirates.
The theme of the story is friendship.
The class picked a theme for the art show.

easy.def: They, and not someone else.
examples: They made lunch themselves.
The kids dressed themselves.
They hurt themselves.

more.def: Used when "they" are the ones who do something and also receive it.
examples: The twins built the fort themselves.
The children dressed themselves.
The birds cleaned themselves in the puddle.

easy.def: After that.
examples: I ate, and then I played.
First wash, then dry.
Then she went home.

more.def: At that time, or next, after something else.
examples: Mix the flour and water, and then add the eggs.
We saw the lightning, and then we heard the thunder.
I was in kindergarten then, and I was very small.

easy.def: An idea that explains something.
examples: I have a theory.
Her theory was funny.
A theory about dinosaurs.

more.def: An idea that tries to explain something.
examples: I have a theory about why the cat sleeps there.
Scientists have a theory about how the moon formed.
His theory was that the dog hid the sock.

easy.def: In that place.
examples: Put the book there.
I will go there.
The cat is over there.

more.def: In or to a place that is not where you are, or at that place just mentioned.
examples: We drove to the beach and played there all afternoon.
Look over there, behind the big oak tree.
The store is closed, so there is no point going.

easy.def: For that reason.
examples: It was raining, so we therefore stayed inside.
I was tired, therefore I went to bed.
He studied; therefore he passed.

more.def: For that reason, as a result of what was just said.
examples: The road was icy, and therefore the bus drove slowly.
She studied hard and therefore did well on the test.
It was cold; therefore we wore our coats.

easy.def: A word for things that are close to you.
examples: These are my shoes.
I like these.
Look at these!

more.def: A word used for more than one person or thing that is near you or has just been mentioned.
examples: These berries are ripe, so we can pick them.
Put these papers in your backpack.
These are the animals we saw at the farm.

easy.def: A word for two or more people or things.
examples: They are my friends.
They play in the yard.
The birds are loud, and they sing.

more.def: A word used for two or more people, animals, or things that have already been talked about.
examples: The twins love swimming, and they practice every Saturday.
I cannot find my gloves, but I think they are in the car.
The farmers were happy because they had a good harvest.

easy.def: Wide from one side to the other.
examples: The book is thick.
The wall is thick.
The ice is thick.

more.def: Having a large distance between two sides, or not flowing easily.
examples: The thick book had five hundred pages.
The soup was thick and hearty.
The ice on the pond was thick enough to skate on.

easy.def: A person who steals.
examples: The thief ran away.
The thief took the bike.
Police caught the thief.

more.def: A person who steals things.
examples: The thief took a bike from the yard.
The guard chased the thief.
In the story, a sneaky thief stole the king's crown.

easy.def: Not thick.
examples: A thin line is on the paper.
The ice is thin.
I read a thin book.

more.def: Not thick or fat, with only a small distance from one side to the other.
examples: A thin layer of ice covered the pond.
The thin book took only a day to read.
She spread a thin coat of butter on the toast.

easy.def: Any object, or something you do not name.
examples: What is that thing?
I packed my things.
The best thing is cake.

more.def: An object, a fact, or an idea that is not named exactly.
examples: There was a strange thing in the box, but I did not know what it was.
The most important thing is to stay safe.
She put all of her things in a bag before the trip.

easy.def: To use your mind.
examples: I think about my pet.
She thinks hard.
We thought of a good plan.

more.def: To use your mind to form ideas or to have an opinion.
examples: I think it will rain before lunch because the clouds are dark.
He is thinking about what to draw for the art show.
What do you think the answer is?

easy.def: Number three in order.
examples: I am third in line.
She won third place.
Today is the third day of camp.

more.def: Coming after the second and before the fourth.
examples: My brother came in third place in the race.
We live on the third floor.
It was the third time we visited the zoo.

easy.def: One more than twelve.
examples: I have thirteen stickers.
My cousin is thirteen.
Thirteen birds sat on the wire.

more.def: The number 13, which comes after twelve and before fourteen.
examples: A baker's dozen means thirteen.
She turns thirteen next month.
Thirteen players sat on the bench.

easy.def: The number 30.
examples: I have thirty stickers.
Thirty days are in June.
There are thirty kids in my class.

more.def: The number that comes after twenty-nine, written 30.
examples: There are thirty students in my class.
June has thirty days.
We walked for thirty minutes.

easy.def: A word for a thing that is close to you.
examples: This is my toy.
I like this.
Look at this!

more.def: A word used to point to a person or thing that is near you or that you are just about to talk about.
examples: This is the book I told you about.
Try this juice, because it is made from fresh pears.
These shoes are too small for me now.

easy.def: A word for things that are not close to you.
examples: Those are my shoes.
Look at those birds.
I like those.

more.def: A word used for more than one person or thing that is farther away or has already been named.
examples: Those mountains in the distance are covered with snow.
Do you remember those cookies we baked last winter?
Those are the books I borrowed from the library.

easy.def: Used to say something that you may not expect.
examples: Though it rained, we had fun.
I am not tired, though it is late.
She smiled, though she was sad.

more.def: In spite of the fact that; although.
examples: Though the hill was steep, the little girl climbed all the way to the top.
We had a great time at the park, though it started to rain.
He kept reading, even though the room was getting dark.

easy.def: An idea in your mind.
examples: I had a happy thought.
She shared her thought.
That is a nice thought.

more.def: An idea or opinion that comes into your mind, or the act of thinking.
examples: I had a funny thought while I was watching the clouds.
After some thought, he chose the blue paint.
Please share your thoughts about the story with the class.

easy.def: The number 1,000.
examples: The stadium holds a thousand people.
A thousand stars are in the sky.
Count to one thousand.

more.def: The number 1,000, which is ten hundreds.
examples: A thousand meters make one kilometer.
Thousands of fans cheered for the team.
The ancient tree is over a thousand years old.

easy.def: A warning that something bad may happen.
examples: The dark clouds were a threat of rain.
A big storm is a threat.
The loud dog is not a real threat.

more.def: Something that could cause harm, or a warning that harm may come.
examples: Dark clouds in the sky were a threat of a storm.
Pollution is a threat to fish in the river.
The wasps were a threat to the picnic.

easy.def: To say you might hurt someone.
examples: The storm threatens the town.
The dog threatened to bark.
Dark clouds threaten rain.

more.def: To say or show that something bad may happen.
examples: Dark clouds threaten rain over the hills.
The big wave threatened the sandcastle.
The coach threatened to cancel practice if we were late.

easy.def: The number 3.
examples: I have three pets.
Three plus one is four.
She is three years old.

more.def: The number 3, which is one more than two.
examples: A triangle has three sides.
The farmer counted three eggs in the nest.
We waited three days for the package.

easy.def: A feeling of great excitement.
examples: The ride gave me a thrill.
Seeing the whale was a thrill.
She felt a thrill.

more.def: A sudden feeling of great excitement and joy.
examples: The roller coaster gave me a thrill.
It was a thrill to see the whale jump.
She felt a thrill when she heard her name called.

easy.def: To make someone very excited.
examples: The show thrilled the children.
The ride thrilled us.
The game thrills me.

more.def: To give someone a feeling of great excitement.
examples: The magic show thrilled the children.
The fast ride thrilled us all.
The big game thrilled the whole town.

easy.def: The front of your neck, or the tube inside.
examples: My throat is sore.
Food goes down my throat.
I have a sore throat.

more.def: The tube inside the neck that carries food and air, or the front of the neck.
examples: Water slid down my throat.
I have a sore throat from yelling.
The doctor looked at my throat.

easy.def: In one side and out the other.
examples: We walked through the door.
The train goes through a tunnel.
Light comes through the window.

more.def: From one end, side, or part of something to the other.
examples: The river flows through the valley and into the sea.
We hiked through the forest to reach the lake.
Sunlight shone through the clouds after the storm.

easy.def: To send something through the air with your hand.
examples: Throw me the ball.
She threw a stick.
I can throw far.

more.def: To send something through the air by moving your arm quickly.
examples: Throw the ball to your partner as gently as you can.
He threw the stick, and the dog ran after it.
She has thrown the football farther than anyone else.

easy.def: The short, thick finger on the side of your hand.
examples: I hurt my thumb.
She sucked her thumb.
I gave a thumbs up.

more.def: The short, thick finger that is on the side of your hand.
examples: I hit my thumb with the hammer.
He gave a thumbs up.
Your thumb helps you hold a pencil.

easy.def: The loud boom you hear in a storm.
examples: The thunder was so loud!
The dog hides when it hears thunder.
Thunder comes after lightning.

more.def: The loud rumbling sound that follows a flash of lightning.
examples: The thunder rattled the windows of the house.
We heard thunder rolling in the distance.
Our dog hides under the bed whenever there is thunder.

easy.def: The day after Wednesday.
examples: Thursday is library day.
We bake bread on Thursday.
Dad comes home on Thursday.

more.def: The day of the week that comes after Wednesday and before Friday.
examples: Thursday is the day our class feeds the school rabbits.
The play opens on Thursday evening.
Next Thursday, the circus comes to town.
